question: Which of the following Articles of the Constitution emphasizes the fundamental duty – “To preserve and protect the sovereignty, unity, and integrity of India”?
solution:
The correct answer is __Art 51A (c)__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Article 51A is a Fundamental Duty in Part IV -A of the Indian Constitution.
 
• The idea of incorporating Fundamental Duties into the Indian constitution was inspired by the Russian Constitution (erstwhile Soviet Union).
 
• They help in promoting the spirit of discipline and patriotism among the citizens.
 
• Additionally, they assist in achieving societal objectives by encouraging active citizen participation instead of the spectator.
 
• Ten Fundamental Duties were added by the 42nd Constitution Amendment Act in 1976 on the recommendation of the Swaran Singh Committee.
 
• Ten duties were originally added, and one more was added in 2002 by the 86th Constitutional Amendment Act.

List of 11 Fundamental Duties under article 51 A:

 
• 51A (a): to abide by the Constitution and respect its ideals and institutions, the National Flag and the National Anthem.
 
• 51A (b): to cherish and follow the noble ideals which inspired our national struggle for freedom.
 
• 51A (c): to uphold and protect** the sovereignty, unity and integrity of India. **Hense Option 1 is correct.
 
• 51A (d): to defend the country and render national service when called upon to do so.
 
• 51A (e): to promote harmony and the spirit of common brotherhood amongst all the people of India transcending religious, linguistic and regional or sectional diversities; to renounce practices derogatory to the dignity of women.
 
• 51A (f): to value and preserve the rich heritage of our composite culture.
 
• 51A (g): to protect and improve the natural environment including forests, lakes, rivers and wild life, and to have compassion for living creatures.
 
• 51A (h): to develop the scientific temper, humanism and the spirit of inquiry and reform.
 
• 51A (i): to safeguard public property and to abjure violence.
 
• 51A (j): to strive towards excellence in all spheres of individual and collective activity so that the nation constantly rises to higher levels of endeavour and achievement.
 
• 51A (k): who is a parent or guardian to provide opportunities for education to his child or, as the case may be, ward between the age of six and fourteen years.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__

__Swaran Singh Committee 1976 Report__

 
• The Swaran Singh Committee was formed in 1976 to examine the working of the Indian Constitution.
 
• The committee's objective was to recommend amendments to the Constitution.
 
• The committee submitted its report in 1976, known as the Swaran Singh Committee Report.
 
• The report proposed several amendments to the Constitution.
 
• It recommended changes in fundamental rights, directive principles of state policy, emergency provisions, and the role of the President.
 
• One significant proposal was the inclusion of the Right to Property as a legal right.
 
• The committee also recommended strengthening the parliamentary system, enhancing the judiciary's role, and improving political parties' functioning.
 
• However, not all of the committee's recommendations were implemented.
 
• The Swaran Singh Committee Report remains a significant document in the constitutional discourse of India.
